epithet: “Would you kill a man for saying, ‘My Lord is Allah’?”
lede: The first of the seven Ḥā Mīm surahs. In Pharaoh’s own court, as the order to kill Mūsā is being discussed, one man who had hidden his faith stands up and speaks. The surah gives him the floor for eighteen ayat — and Abū Bakr once shouted his words at the Kaʿbah, with his hands on a man who was strangling the Prophet ﷺ.

names.name: Ghāfir
names.note: From its third ayah, where Allah is named “Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance”.

names.name: al-Muʾmin
names.note: After the believing man of Pharaoh’s household. This is the name Ibn al-Jawzī heads it with, and al-Qurṭubī gives both. It is also called al-Ṭawl, Abundance, from the same third ayah, and Ḥā Mīm al-Muʾmin.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah and Qatādah; a report from Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah excepts two ayat as Madinan. Ibn al-Jawzī cites al-Zajjāj: all of the Ḥawāmīm came down in Makkah. It is the first of the seven, which stand together in the muṣḥaf as they came down together; the traditional order places it sixtieth.
revelation.when: The later years in Makkah, when there was open talk of killing the Prophet ﷺ

evidence.quote: وهي مَكِّيَّةٌ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، ومُجاهِدٌ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وقَتادَةُ. وحُكِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ وقَتادَةُ أنَّ فِيها آَيَتَيْنِ نَزَلَتا بِالمَدِينَةِ
قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: "آلُ حم" دِيبَاجُ الْقُرْآنِ

setting: The seven surahs that begin with Ḥā Mīm run from here to al-Aḥqāf. Ibn Masʿūd called them the brocade of the Qurʾan. They share an opening — the letters, and then the sending down of the Book — and a subject: the Qurʾan itself, and those who dispute about it. This one states the theme in its fourth ayah: “None dispute concerning the signs of Allah but those who disbelieve; so do not be deceived by their going to and fro in the land.”

By the time it came down the dispute in Makkah had turned murderous. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr was asked what was the worst thing the idolaters ever did to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: “I saw ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ come to the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying, put his cloak round his neck and choke him with it, hard. Then Abū Bakr came and thrust him away, and said: ‘Would you kill a man because he says, My Lord is Allah — when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?’”

Those are the words of a man in this surah. Pharaoh has said, “Let me kill Mūsā.” And a believer from Pharaoh’s own family, who had been concealing his faith, speaks — carefully at first, as one of them: if he is a liar, his lie is on himself, and if he is truthful, some of what he warns you of will strike you. Then more and more openly, as it becomes clear that they will not listen: “My people, I fear for you a day like the day of the confederates… My people, this worldly life is only a passing enjoyment, and the Hereafter is the lasting home… How is it that I call you to salvation and you call me to the Fire?” He ends: “You will remember what I say to you. I entrust my affair to Allah.” And Allah protected him from the evils they plotted.

Around that story the surah sets two scenes in heaven and two in the Fire. The angels who bear the Throne ask forgiveness for the believers and their families. And the people of the Fire beg its keepers to ask their Lord to lighten a single day.

occasions.title: Abū Bakr at the Kaʿbah
occasions.text: ʿUrwah asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: tell me the worst thing the idolaters did to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: “While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying in the courtyard of the Kaʿbah, ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ came, seized his shoulder, twisted his garment round his neck and throttled him severely. Abū Bakr came, took him by the shoulder and pushed him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: ‘Would you kill a man because he says, My Lord is Allah, when he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord?’”

aim: To deal with those who dispute about the signs of Allah — by reasoning with them, and calling them back to the truth.
themes: The angels’ prayer for the believers

outline.title: The Book, and those who dispute it
outline.summary: Ḥā Mīm. The sending down of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the Knowing: Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, severe in punishment, Owner of abundance. None dispute the signs of Allah but those who disbelieve; let their movement through the land not deceive you. Before them the people of Nūḥ denied, and the confederates after them; every nation plotted to seize its messenger.

outline.title: The prayer of the angels
outline.summary: Those who bear the Throne, and those around it, glorify their Lord with praise, believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: “Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge; forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and shield them from the punishment of the Blaze. Admit them to the Gardens of Eden You promised them, and the righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring.”

outline.title: The Day of Meeting
outline.summary: Those who disbelieved will be told: “Allah’s abhorrence of you was greater than your abhorrence of yourselves.” They say: “Our Lord, twice You made us die and twice You gave us life; is there any way out?” The Day they come forth, nothing of them hidden from Allah: “Whose is the dominion today?” — “Allah’s, the One, the Subduer.” Warn them of the Day drawing near, when hearts are at the throats. He knows the treachery of the eyes, and what the breasts conceal.

outline.title: The believer of Pharaoh’s household
outline.summary: We sent Mūsā to Pharaoh, Hāmān and Qārūn. Pharaoh said, “Let me kill Mūsā.” A believing man of Pharaoh’s family, who had hidden his faith, said: “Would you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is Allah’? My people, yours is the dominion today — but who will help us against Allah’s might if it comes? I fear for you the Day of Calling. This life is only a passing enjoyment; the Hereafter is the abiding home. I call you to the Almighty, the Forgiving. I entrust my affair to Allah.” So Allah protected him — and Pharaoh’s people were encompassed by the worst punishment: the Fire, to which they are exposed morning and evening.

outline.title: In the Fire, and the promise of help
outline.summary: They argue in the Fire, the weak with the proud. They say to the keepers of Hell, “Call upon your Lord to lighten for us one day of the punishment.” We shall surely help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day the witnesses stand. So be patient: the promise of Allah is true. Ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify your Lord with praise, evening and morning.

outline.title: “Call upon Me”
outline.summary: Those who dispute the signs of Allah without authority have nothing in their breasts but a pride they will never satisfy. The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. Your Lord has said: “Call upon Me; I will answer you” (40:60). It is Allah who made the night for you to rest in and the day to see by; who made the earth a dwelling and the sky a canopy, and shaped you and made your shapes fair. He is the Living; there is no god but He — so call on Him, making the religion sincerely His.

outline.title: Belief at the sight of punishment
outline.summary: Have you seen those who dispute the signs of Allah — how they are turned away? When the shackles are on their necks, and the chains, they will be dragged through boiling water. So be patient. We sent messengers before you: of some We have told you, and of some We have not. When their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they exulted in the knowledge they had. And when they saw Our might they said, “We believe in Allah alone.” But their belief did not benefit them once they had seen Our might.

keyAyah.why: A command and a promise in one line. The Prophet ﷺ recited it and said: supplication is worship.

virtues.text: “Supplication is worship.” Then he recited: “And your Lord has said: Call upon Me; I will answer you. Those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled.”
virtues.grade: Ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ, said al-Tirmidhī; ṣaḥīḥ according to al-Albānī

before: Al-Zumar ended with the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord. Ghāfir shows them again, and tells what they are asking for.
after: Ghāfir ends with people who exulted in what they knew. Fuṣṣilat opens with the knowledge that had now come to Quraysh — a Book whose ayat are set out in detail, in Arabic — and how they turned from it.
